Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-15 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Orbit ML Lead), Tomás Alvarez (Orbit Platform Eng), Jill Kapoor (Orbit PM)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect): weekly checkpoint to review scorecard regressions and run a rollback/fallback drill; discussed prompt-level fixes and security questions, agreed on next steps.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay uh hi everyone thanks for carving out time, Maya from Redwood here, we'll kick off. Just to confirm the agenda — regression heatmap, rollback drill results, prompt pruning, then security quick Qs.
[00:21] Lena Park: Hey Maya, hi Diego. Yep that sounds right, we also want to see the logs from the fallback test, like how the KV cache behaved.
[00:35] Diego Rivera: Cool, Diego here. Quick note, transcription might mangle names, "KV" sometimes comes out as "key vee" in the export :)
[00:44] Tomás Alvarez: hah, yeah noticed that. Also FYI we had one spike in latency during the midnight batch on Wednesday.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Right ok, Diego can you share the regression heatmap first?
[01:10] Diego Rivera: Sure pulling the shared sheet — bear with me, um the biggest cluster is prompt set B3, where we saw a 4.2% drop in semantic score vs baseline, and some guardrail flips where benign responses got flagged. Timestamping note: some rows are auto-tagged.
[01:34] Jill Kapoor: When you say guardrail flips you mean false positives? Because product folks saw customer-facing rejections.
[01:46] Diego Rivera: Yeah mostly false positives — output was safe but the safety classifier tripped on certain templates in B3, especially those with code-like snippets.
[01:58] Lena Park: That's concerning. Our acceptance criteria was <1% false-positive rate. This is 4x.
[02:10] Maya Chen: Understood. Two things — one, prompt pruning for B3 could reduce FP. Two, fallback/rollback to a slightly older model variant during the spike. We ran a rollback drill earlier today; Diego, can you walk through results?
[02:30] Diego Rivera: Yep. We executed a simulated rollback from v2.3.1-quant to v2.2.9-rt at around simulated t=0. Drill lasted 8 minutes, routing policy switched to fallback policy FBR-1, requests auto-routed to dedicated pool 1. Latency delta was +18ms on tail but CPU/GPU utilization smoothed out, and error rate dropped to baseline.
[02:58] Tomás Alvarez: Wait +18ms tail — how's user impact for our worst-case? Our SLO is 200ms p99 for chat.
[03:11] Diego Rivera: Worst-case p99 during rollback peaked at 230ms for about 30s in the sim, then back to 195ms. So temporarily over SLO but short lived.
[03:26] Jill Kapoor: That seems acceptable if we communicate it in the SLA playbook. But the bigger issue is whether fallback changes content quality for key flows.
[03:40] Maya Chen: Good call. We measured a small accuracy delta on intent classification for billing flows — 1.1% drop. Diego, that's in the shared sheet too, right?
[03:51] Diego Rivera: Yep it's row 78-82. Also note that when we switched, prefix cache invalidation caused a cold start for some keys which contributed to latency spike. We can tune cache TTLs to mitigate.
[04:14] Lena Park: Can we do a rolling invalidate instead of full purge? That would help.
[04:22] Diego Rivera: Yes, rolling invalidation is possible and we recommend it for noisy keys. We'll propose the TTLs.
[04:32] Maya Chen: Switching tracks to prompt sets — Lena you sent a 500-sample failure set last night, correct?
[04:44] Lena Park: Yep, uploaded to the drive under /orbit/poc/failures/latest, but the file name got trimmed so the transcriber shows it as "latest_fail" so FYI.
[04:56] Diego Rivera: I reviewed, most failures are from long-context where the model hallucinates an ID. We've flagged 3 prompt templates that amplify hallucination: A12, B3, C7.
[05:12] Jill Kapoor: Are these templates user-facing or internal? If user-facing we need immediate guardrails.
[05:21] Lena Park: Mostly user-facing, the billing summary prompt is part of the widget.
[05:28] Maya Chen: Then prioritize B3 pruning + a guardrail that requires deterministic fields for IDs. We can add canonicalization and post-processing to scrub hallucinated identifiers.
[05:41] Tomás Alvarez: How intrusive is that change developer-side? We want minimal frontend changes.
[05:49] Diego Rivera: Minimal — we added a post-processing step in the middleware that compares candidate IDs against a prefix list via KV lookups. If mismatch, trigger clarification flow. That reduced hallucination by ~67% in sim.
[06:06] Lena Park: Nice. About scoring — our scorecard uses a weighted metric: semantic accuracy 60%, safety 25%, latency 15%. With rollback, safety improved but semantic dipped slightly. We need to see a new threshold that captures business impact.
[06:24] Maya Chen: Agreed. Action: Diego and Lena to propose adjusted weighting scenarios and run sensitivity analysis.
[06:34] Jill Kapoor: Quick question on security — we need SOC2 attestation and specifics on KMS integration. Is Redwood's private deploy using customer-managed keys?
[06:46] Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and we can integrate Okta for SSO. For hosted we encrypt at rest with our KMS but offer bring-your-own-key for Private. We'll send the security pack after this call.
[07:00] Tomás Alvarez: Can you also include audit log retention options? We have retention policies that require longer than default.
[07:09] Maya Chen: Yes, Diego will include log retention tiers and export paths.
[07:16] Diego Rivera: On that note, I want to call out one nuance — when you run dedicated pools in VPC, the audit logs route slightly differently, sometimes adding a small lag to ingestion. We'll document those trade-offs.
[07:33] Lena Park: Trade-offs are fine as long as we can guarantee tamper-evidence and chain-of-custody for logs.
[07:42] Maya Chen: Understood. Back to the rollback drill: we also tested fallback to a smaller quantized variant to save cost during peak — that saved about 12% unit cost but quality dipped more than the regular fallback.
[07:57] Jill Kapoor: So cost vs quality — we need a policy that says "acceptable for non-critical flows".
[08:06] Diego Rivera: Yep that's what the routing policy config is for — route to cost-optimized model for non-payment flows, keep high-fidelity for billing and auth.
[08:17] Tomás Alvarez: On the latency spike Wednesday, any theory?
[08:22] Diego Rivera: Early signs show a hot key pattern from a cron job and then prefix cache thrashing, plus a simultaneous autoscale event. The combination caused a tail spike.
[08:36] Lena Park: So mitigation: throttle cron, add rate-limit on that key, and increase burst capacity for autoscale.
[08:45] Maya Chen: We'll provide recommended autoscale policies tuned for your request distribution.
[08:52] Jill Kapoor: I have one user-experience concern — during fallback some responses became more verbose, affecting widget layout. Can we cap tokens?
[09:01] Diego Rivera: Yes, model-parallel parameters let you cap generation length per route. We can set hard cap for the widget.
[09:09] Maya Chen: Quick check — any blockers from Orbit on running the deeper benchmarks?
[09:15] Lena Park: We need a little more visibility into the test harness — specifically how you compute semantic score. Our team wants the evaluation script to be open so we can reproduce.
[09:25] Diego Rivera: We can share the evaluation harness and a reproducible Docker image. Note that some scoring uses a proprietary rubric for edge cases, but we'll annotate it heavily.
[09:36] Tomás Alvarez: Please do. Also, do you have any recommended quantization profiles for our T4-ish fleet?
[09:44] Diego Rivera: For T4 we'd recommend 4-bit quant with per-channel calibration, but run head-to-head because different models behave differently with q4. Diego (note: same) will attach the quant profiles.
[09:58] Maya Chen: We're about halfway, want to summarize next steps and then run through the rollback log snippets live?
[10:06] Lena Park: Yes please show the logs.
[10:12] Diego Rivera: Sharing screen — logs show the routing handoff at 00:00:14, TTL invalidation at 00:00:18, and p99 spike until 00:00:44. You can see the key hashes in the trace but obfuscated by default.
[10:30] Tomás Alvarez: The obfuscation is fine, but can we get a redacted trace with full keys for our infra team under NDA?
[10:39] Maya Chen: Yes we can; will require an NDA amendment — I'll coordinate with legal.
[10:47] Jill Kapoor: Did the rollback introduce any request ordering issues? We observed one session with out-of-order messages.
[10:55] Diego Rivera: One instance, yes — caused by in-flight KV cache invalidation and async request routing; we recommend session sticky routing during rollout window.
[11:09] Lena Park: Good catch. We'll add sticky routing as a requirement for sensitive flows.
[11:16] Maya Chen: Okay let's close with clear owners. Diego — run two more rollback sims and share logs + TTL recommendations.
[11:25] Diego Rivera: Got it.
[11:27] Maya Chen: Lena — share the 500-sample failure set with priority tags.
[11:31] Lena Park: Will do.
[11:33] Maya Chen: Tomás — SSO metadata and retention policy ticket.
[11:36] Tomás Alvarez: On it.
[11:38] Maya Chen: Jill — please collate widget UX issues and send prioritized list.
[11:42] Jill Kapoor: Yes.
[11:44] Maya Chen: I'll send pricing for dedicated scenarios and the security pack. We'll reconvene for the runbook review next week. Thanks all.
[11:52] Diego Rivera: Thanks everyone.
[11:55] Lena Park: Thanks.

End of meeting.
